audit_findings.title: Current debt interest is absent from the FY2025 OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.0 million debt at 5.48% implies $1.206 million annual pretax interest; replacing FY2025's $0.077 million interest produces an approximately $0.813 million incremental after-tax annual cost and an approximately $11.4 million, or $0.74 per-share, reduction in base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the equity-level OE anchor because this method retains interest expense instead of deducting debt principal in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had $ 0 outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch: the $16.4 million anchor reflects a debt-free year, while $22.0 million was outstanding at the valuation date. At fixed valuation assumptions, normalizing the interest would reduce base value by about 4.8%. The precise run rate remains sensitive to debt duration, repayments, fees and tax treatment.
audit_findings.action: Replace embedded FY2025 interest with the after-tax forecast interest and fees on the June 2026 borrowing schedule, then rerun every scenario without deducting the same debt principal in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Large unfinished expansion spending may be excluded while its growth is valued
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest filed estimate $50.500 million less $38.917 million cumulative cash paid leaves $11.583 million; equivalent to $0.75 per diluted share and 4.9% of the $238 million base equity value if entirely omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncharged remaining expansion cash outflows would reduce projected OE or require a separate equity-value adjustment; associated borrowing also increases future interest retained in equity OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company currently estimates investing approximately $48,000.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q reduces the unresolved amount from the audit's roughly $27.1 million to $11.583 million, but confirms that the project was unfinished and increased capacity was not expected to begin until January 2027. It is not demonstrated that the DCF omitted this spending or assumed its benefits, but the remaining amount is large enough to affect the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $38.917 million paid and $11.583 million remaining to forecast OE, commissioning dates and scenario growth; identify maintenance versus expansion spending and rerun with remaining outlays, returns and financing interest represented exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The Simple Mills gain may have been terminalized and double counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.407 million pretax gain; approximately $2.398 million after the filed 29.6% FY2025 tax rate; if included in the anchor, approximately $33.6 million or $2.18 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring gain retained in anchor OE is grown and terminalized, while the related sale proceeds also remain within the latest cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company received cash proceeds of $ 5,206 and recognized a gain on the sale of investment of $ 3,407 during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the gain and $5.206 million proceeds, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation removed the gain. If retained, the gain equals about 14.6% of the $16.4 million anchor after tax and would materially overstate value through both terminalization and potential double counting.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.407 million gain and tax effect through the FY2025 OE worksheet, remove it if present, and confirm that the $5.206 million proceeds enter valuation only through the June 2026 cash balance.

audit_findings.title: The herd arrangement may fall outside the calculator’s capital rules
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.870 million cow purchases; $2.666 million of related current and long-term assets at June 30, 2026; complete net cash effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cow purchases, principal recoveries, strategic interest income and replacement or mortality spending can enter different cash-flow sections even though they form one operating supply arrangement.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company records the purchases of dairy cows as investing outflows, principal payments received as investing inflows and interest income as operating inflows on the statement of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification mismatch is demonstrated, but no demonstrated valuation error follows without the OE worksheet and contractual payment schedule. Omitting purchases or replacement capital would overstate value, while omitting principal receipts or economically operating interest would understate it. The record cannot quantify the recurring net effect.
audit_findings.action: Build a contract-level cash schedule through the amended 36-month term, including purchases, principal receipts, interest, mortality, replacements and the nominal repurchase right, then apply one consistent OE treatment to the entire arrangement.

audit_findings.title: Supposedly non-routine legal costs have recurred
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.200 million pretax in FY2025, $4.500 million in FY2024 and $0.375 million in the first half of 2026; a full FY2025 add-back would equal approximately $4.365 million after tax and approximately $61.2 million or $3.97 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any normalization directly changes anchor OE and is then propagated through explicit-period growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company incurred approximately $6,200 of legal and professional fees associated with Danone’s unsolicited purchase proposal and non-routine stockholder action during 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurrence across three periods demonstrates that treating all FY2025 expense as a one-off would be unsupported. Conversely, retaining all $6.2 million could understate sustainable OE if the proposal, litigation and cooperation-related work has substantially ended. Because the possible adjustment is about 26.6% of the current anchor after tax, the treatment is materially consequential.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2024-2026 charges through OE, separate continuing governance and litigation costs from transaction-specific costs, document the post-cooperation run rate, and rerun scenarios using the supported normalized amount.

audit_findings.title: The 2021 OE figure appears to contain a unit-scaling error
audit_findings.magnitude: Apparent 1,000-fold error: $4,031.5 million versus an implied $4.0315 million, a $4,027.4685 million difference
audit_findings.mechanism: Affects historical trend, too-hard rationale and possibly RONTA diagnostics, but not the latest-actual $16.4 million OE anchor or the stated scenario inputs.
audit_findings.evidence: Unless otherwise noted herein, all amounts in this Form 10-K are in thousands, except per share numbers.
audit_findings.explanation: The scale is highly indicative of an error, although the original 2021 calculation must confirm it. It is not material to the reported intrinsic values because the valuation explicitly anchors to FY2025 OE, and the independent negative FY2018 and FY2019 observations still support the too-hard designation. Correcting it therefore does not change the scenario cash flows as supplied.
audit_findings.action: Verify the 2021 source units and rerun the trend, too-hard and RONTA diagnostics only; escalate for a valuation rerun solely if the corrected diagnostics are shown to alter the anchor or growth scenarios.
